```{ojs}
// Shared CMIP6 cache base URL — defined here (was scoped to CR-097 before)
// so the shared `cmip6_future_data` cell below can use it. Same path used
// by every Future Projections sub-section (CR-097, Period maps, and future
// ridges / climatology when those land).
cr097_base = "https://digital-atlas.s3.amazonaws.com/domain=climate/type=hazard-indices/source=nex-gddp-cmip6/region=africa/processing=timeseries_mean_month/timeframe=3months"
```

```{ojs}
// Single DuckDB-WASM client for every Future Projections sub-section.
// One client + one fetch = parquets pulled once per scope change instead
// of once per sub-section. Per-plot clients are unnecessary here because
// each sub-section runs a single in-memory filter, not a separate SQL
// query (see `cmip6_future_data` below).
db_cmip6_future = DuckDBClient.of()
```

```{ojs}
// Section-gate for Future Projections — fires when ANY sub-section
// scrolls into view. Sub-sections that land later (climatology table…)
// should be OR'd in here too so they piggy-back on the same fetch.
futureProjectionsVisible = (cr097Visible || periodMapsVisible || periodRidgesVisible || periodPolarVisible)
```

```{ojs}
// ============================================================================
// CMIP6 cache variable-set policy
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// To keep the per-scope fetch small, the cache pulls a CORE set of climate
// variables by default (TAVG / TMAX / TMIN / PTOT). Additional hazard
// variables (SPEI-03 / SPEI-12 / NTx35 / NTx40 / NDWS / NDWL0 / THI-max /
// NDD) are pulled on demand — the moment any section's variable selector
// lands on an extra, that variable is added to the SQL `WHERE hazard IN
// (...)` clause and the cache re-fetches under the new scope × variable
// set. Going back to a core variable drops the extra (the union recomputes
// each time the OJS cell re-evaluates), so the cache stays minimal.
// ============================================================================
cmip6_core_variables = ["TAVG","TMAX","TMIN","PTOT"]
```

```{ojs}
// Full variable list shown in Period maps + Period ridges + Period
// polar variable selectors. Items outside `cmip6_core_variables` are
// "(opt-in)" — selecting one triggers a re-fetch under a widened
// hazard filter. Core 4 are always cached.
// SPEI is NOT here — SPEI is observational-only (CHIRPS-derived); the
// CMIP6 projection parquet does not ship it. See main notebook's
// `futureHazards = hazards_obj.filter(!startsWith SPEI)` for the
// canonical filter. Use the P6 (observational decade maps) selector
// to access SPEI.
cmip6FutureVariableValues = [
  "TAVG","TMAX","TMIN","PTOT",
  "NTx35","NTx40",
  "NDWS","NDWL0",
  "THI-max","HSH-max",
]
```

```{ojs}
cmip6FutureVariableFormat = v => ({
  TAVG:      "TAVG — avg temp",
  TMAX:      "TMAX — mean daily max",
  TMIN:      "TMIN — mean daily min",
  PTOT:      "PTOT — precipitation",
  "NTx35":   "NTx35 — days > 35 °C (opt-in)",
  "NTx40":   "NTx40 — days > 40 °C (opt-in)",
  "NDWS":    "NDWS — water-stress days (opt-in)",
  "NDWL0":   "NDWL0 — waterlogging days (opt-in)",
  "THI-max": "THI-max — livestock heat-stress (opt-in)",
  "HSH-max": "HSH-max — heat-stress hours (opt-in)",
}[v] ?? v)
```

```{ojs}
// Union of: core 4 + whichever variable each sub-section is currently
// asking for. Section-controls cells declare their default values up-front
// so this never crashes on first run — the union just produces the core
// set until any control resolves to an extra.
//
// Returns a stable `|`-separated string instead of an array so OJS sees
// no change when the set's CONTENT is identical (toggling a variable
// from one core member to another e.g. TAVG → PTOT). Arrays are object
// references; OJS would treat every re-computation as a new value and
// re-fetch the parquet cache. Strings compare by value → no spurious
// refetch.
cmip6_active_variables = {
  const set = new Set(cmip6_core_variables);
  const add = v => { if (typeof v === "string" && v.length) set.add(v); };
  // Reach into each section's `viewof` value reactively.
  try { add(cr097_controls?.variable); }       catch (e) { /* not visible yet */ }
  try { add(periodMaps_controls?.variable); }  catch (e) { /* not visible yet */ }
  try { add(periodRidges_controls?.variable); } catch (e) { /* not visible yet */ }
  try { add(periodPolar_controls?.variable); }  catch (e) { /* not visible yet */ }
  return [...set].sort().join("|");
}
```

```{ojs}
// ============================================================================
// SHARED CMIP6 FUTURE-PROJECTION CACHE
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// One query for the whole Future Projections section. Pulls every variable
// × season × scenario × period × admin1 in the current geographic scope, then
// every downstream sub-section (CR-097 threshold map, Period maps, future
// ridges, future climatology table…) filters in-memory rather than issuing
// its own parquet query. Re-runs only when `globalScopeInfo` changes — never
// on a variable / season / SSP toggle.
//
// Row volume in scope (SSA worst case): ~600 admin1s × 4 hazards × 5 seasons
// × 4 SSPs × 4 periods ≈ 192k rows. Memory footprint ≈ 10–15 MB — within
// DuckDB-WASM + browser comfort. Single-country scopes are dramatically
// smaller (~6k rows for KEN).
// ============================================================================
cmip6_future_data = {
  if (!futureProjectionsVisible) return [];
  const { iso3List } = globalScopeInfo;
  const iso3Where = iso3List.length === 1
    ? `iso3 = '${iso3List[0]}'`
    : `iso3 IN (${iso3List.map(c => `'${c}'`).join(",")})`;
  // Variable filter: core 4 + any extras currently selected in sub-sections.
  // SQL-side filtering caps the byte volume — additional hazard variables
  // (heat-days / drought indices) cost zero bandwidth until a selector
  // actually lands on them. `cmip6_active_variables` is now a stable
  // pipe-joined string (so toggles within the cached set don't refetch);
  // split back into an array for the SQL builder.
  const hazardIn = cmip6_active_variables.split("|")
    .map(v => `'${v.replace(/'/g, "''")}'`)
    .join(",");
  // Broad SELECT — season + scenario filters stay client-side (cheap on
  // the in-memory cache). iso3 + hazard are filtered server-side so
  // DuckDB-WASM can prune row-groups and bytes (single-iso3: `iso3 =
  // '<X>'` form per the pushdown memory note).
  const makeUnion = (url, period) => `
    SELECT admin1_name, iso3, scenario, '${period}' AS period,
           hazard AS variable, season,
           mean_anomaly, sd_anomaly, mean
    FROM read_parquet('${url}')
    WHERE ${iso3Where} AND hazard IN (${hazardIn}) AND admin1_name IS NOT NULL`;
  const url = (p) =>
    `${cr097_base}/period=${p}/baseline=1995-2014/variable=ensemble_season_timeseries.parquet`;

  // Query the 4 future periods first. These are the canonical files that
  // CR-097 + Period maps need; if this fails the section is broken anyway.
  const futurePeriods = ["2021-2040","2041-2060","2061-2080","2081-2100"];
  const futureSql = futurePeriods.map(p => makeUnion(url(p), p)).join(" UNION ALL ");
  const futureRows = Array.from(await db_cmip6_future.query(futureSql));

  // Try to add the 1995-2014 historic parquet for the ridges + climatology
  // baseline reference. If it fails (missing on S3, schema drift, CORS),
  // log + continue with futures-only — ridges drops its baseline ridge
  // gracefully (the `havePeriods` filter in the render block already keeps
  // periods with ≥2 admin1s of data and drops the rest).
  let historicRows = [];
  try {
    historicRows = Array.from(await db_cmip6_future.query(
      makeUnion(url("1995-2014"), "1995-2014")));
  } catch (err) {
    // Surface to console only; don't throw — the rest of the section
    // works without the baseline ridge.
    if (typeof console !== "undefined") console.warn(
      "[sandbox] 1995-2014 historic parquet fetch failed — baseline ridge will be omitted.",
      err && err.message ? err.message : err);
  }
  return [...historicRows, ...futureRows];
}
```

```{ojs}
  "R:EAF": ["BDI","COM","DJI","ERI","ETH","KEN","MDG","MOZ","MUS","MWI","RWA","SOM","SSD","SYC","TZA","UGA"],
  "R:CAF": ["CAF","CMR","COD","COG","GAB","GNQ","STP","TCD"],
  "R:SAF": ["AGO","BWA","LSO","NAM","SWZ","ZAF","ZMB","ZWE"],
  "R:NAF": ["DZA","EGY","ESH","LBY","MAR","SDN","TUN"],
})
```

```{ojs}
// Derived: is single country or region? iso3 list for the query.
globalScopeInfo = {
  const scope = globalScope;
  const isCountry = !scope.startsWith("R:");
  const REGIONS = globalRegionDefs;
  const ALL_ISO3 = Object.values(REGIONS).flat();
  const SSA = [...REGIONS["R:WAF"],...REGIONS["R:EAF"],...REGIONS["R:CAF"],...REGIONS["R:SAF"]];
  const iso3List = isCountry ? [scope]
    : scope === "R:SSA" ? SSA
    : scope === "R:AFR" ? ALL_ISO3
    : (REGIONS[scope] ?? [scope]);
  return { isCountry, iso3List, scope };
}
```

```{ojs}
// Derived: single iso3 for sections that don't support region scopes (P1-P5).
// If the user picks a region, P1-P5 fall back to the first iso3 in the region
// that ALSO appears in `obs_country_codes` (i.e. has observational data on S3).
// Some region member countries (GMB / GNB / LBR / BDI / COM / etc.) don't have
// observational parquets so we skip past them.
globalSingleCountry = globalScopeInfo.isCountry
  ? globalScopeInfo.scope
  : (globalScopeInfo.iso3List.find(c => obs_country_codes.includes(c)) ?? "KEN")
```

```{ojs}
// Section-gate: defer the ~80 MB CMIP6 fetch until the CR-097 placeholder
// scrolls within 300 px of the viewport. Until then `cr097Visible = false`
// and `cr097_data = []` so no network traffic happens.
cr097Visible = sectionVisible("plotCR097", "300px");
```

```{ojs}
// In-memory filter on the shared `cmip6_future_data` cache. No SQL → no
// parquet refetch when the user changes variable / season / SSP. CR-097
// projects mean_anomaly onto a single `pmean` column to keep the rest of
// the section unchanged.
cr097_data = {
  if (!cr097Visible) return [];
  if (!cmip6_future_data.length) return [];
  const { variable, season, ssp } = cr097_controls;
  const ssps = Array.isArray(ssp) && ssp.length ? ssp : ["ssp245"];
  const sspSet = new Set(ssps);
  return cmip6_future_data
    .filter(d => d.variable === variable && d.season === season && sspSet.has(d.scenario))
    .map(d => ({
      admin1_name: d.admin1_name,
      iso3:        d.iso3,
      scenario:    d.scenario,
      period:      d.period,
      pmean:       Number(d.mean_anomaly),
    }));
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
{
  [cr097_controls, globalScopeInfo, globalMapLevel, globalAdmin1, cr097_data,
   globalTopoA1, globalTopoA0, width];
  renderToDiv("plotCR097", () => {
  const { variable, season, showTable } = cr097_controls;
  const { isCountry, iso3List, scope }  = globalScopeInfo;
  const mapLevel   = globalMapLevel;
  const ssps       = Array.isArray(cr097_controls.ssp) && cr097_controls.ssp.length
    ? cr097_controls.ssp : ["ssp245"];
  const thresholds = Array.isArray(cr097_controls.threshold) && cr097_controls.threshold.length
    ? [...cr097_controls.threshold].sort((a,b) => a-b) : [1.5];
  const sspLabels  = { ssp126:"SSP1-2.6", ssp245:"SSP2-4.5", ssp370:"SSP3-7.0", ssp585:"SSP5-8.5" };

  // Country → always admin1. Region → follow toggle (default admin0).
  const useAdmin1Map = isCountry ? true : (mapLevel === "admin1");

  // Colour scale: 5 bins + "not within century" grey.
  const periodColours = {
    "2021-2040": "#e31a1c",
    "2041-2060": "#fd8d3c",
    "2061-2080": "#fecc5c",
    "2081-2100": "#ffffb2",
    null:        "#cccccc",
  };
  const periodLabels = {
    "2021-2040": "2021–2040 (earliest)",
    "2041-2060": "2041–2060",
    "2061-2080": "2061–2080",
    "2081-2100": "2081–2100 (latest)",
    null:        "Threshold not reached by 2100",
  };

  // Loading state — data not yet arrived.
  if (!cr097_data || !cr097_data.length) return htl.html`<p style="color:#888;font-style:italic;padding:12px 0;">
    ⏳ Fetching CMIP6 future-projection parquets (DuckDB-WASM, ~20 MB across 4 files — may take 15–30 s)…
  </p>`;

  // Helper: first period >= threshold.
  const firstCrossing = (rows, t) => {
    const sorted = [...rows].sort((a,b) => a.period.localeCompare(b.period));
    return sorted.find(d => Number(d.pmean) >= t)?.period ?? null;
  };

  // Admin1 rows always fetched. For admin0/region view: aggregate to iso3 per (scenario,period).
  // Aggregation key reflects map level — admin1_name for admin1 view, iso3 for admin0.
  const aggData = useAdmin1Map
    ? cr097_data.map(d => ({ join_key: d.admin1_name, scenario: d.scenario, period: d.period, pmean: Number(d.pmean) }))
    : [...d3.group(cr097_data, d => `${d.iso3}|${d.scenario}|${d.period}`)].map(([k, rs]) => {
        const [jk, scenario, period] = k.split("|");
        return { join_key: jk, scenario, period, pmean: d3.mean(rs, d => Number(d.pmean)) };
      });

  const byScenario = d3.group(aggData, d => d.scenario);

  // join_key — admin1_name or iso3
  const joinKey = d => d.join_key;

  // Select topojson layer and feature key based on map level.
  const useAdmin1 = useAdmin1Map;
  const allFeatures = useAdmin1
    ? topojson.feature(globalTopoA1,    globalTopoA1.objects["atlas_gaul24_a1_africa"]).features
    : topojson.feature(globalTopoA0, globalTopoA0.objects["atlas_gaul24_a0_africa"]).features;
  const featureProp = useAdmin1Map ? "admin1_name" : "iso3";

  // Filter features to current scope.
  const countryFeatures = allFeatures.filter(f => iso3List.includes(f.properties.iso3));
  const selAdmin1 = useAdmin1 ? (globalAdmin1 ?? []) : [];
  const features = selAdmin1.length > 0
    ? countryFeatures.filter(f => selAdmin1.includes(f.properties[featureProp]))
    : countryFeatures;

  // Table mode: render crossing table instead of maps.
  if (showTable) {
    const keys = [...new Set(aggData.map(d => d.join_key))].sort();
    const keyLabel = useAdmin1Map ? "Admin1" : "Country";
    const th = `padding:4px 8px;text-align:left;border-bottom:2px solid #999;font-size:0.8em;background:#eee;white-space:nowrap;`;
    const td = `padding:3px 8px;border-bottom:1px solid #eee;font-size:0.8em;white-space:nowrap;`;
    return htl.html`<div style="overflow-x:auto;margin-top:6px;">
      <p style="font-size:0.83em;color:#777;margin:2px 0 4px;">
        ${scope} · ${variable} · ${season} · vs 1995–2014 baseline · first 20-yr period crossing threshold
      </p>
      <table style="border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;">
        <thead><tr>
          <th style="${th}">${keyLabel}</th>
          ${ssps.flatMap(s => thresholds.map(t =>
            htl.html`<th style="${th}">${sspLabels[s]} ≥+${t}°C</th>`
          ))}
        </tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          ${keys
            .filter(k => selAdmin1.length === 0 || selAdmin1.includes(k))
            .map(k => htl.html`<tr>
            <td style="${td}">${k}</td>
            ${ssps.flatMap(s => {
              const sRows = d3.group(byScenario.get(s) ?? [], joinKey);
              return thresholds.map(t => {
                const cross = firstCrossing(sRows.get(k) ?? [], t);
                return htl.html`<td style="${td};color:${periodColours[cross ?? null]};">
                  ${periodLabels[cross ?? null]}
                </td>`;
              });
            })}
          </tr>`)}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>`;
  }

  if (!features.length) return htl.html`<p style="color:#c00">
    No map features for <strong>${scope}</strong> (${aggData.length} data rows, ${countryFeatures.length} topojson features before filter).
    Check that iso3List = [${iso3List.join(",")}] matches topojson iso3 property.
  </p>`;

  // Facet dimensions: cols = SSPs, rows = thresholds.
  const nCols  = Math.max(ssps.length, 1);
  const nRows  = Math.max(thresholds.length, 1);
  const labelW = 52;  // left label column
  const facetW = Math.max(160, Math.floor((width - labelW - nCols * 2) / nCols));
  const facetH = Math.round(facetW * 0.85);
  const proj0  = d3.geoMercator().fitSize([facetW - 12, facetH - 24],
    { type: "FeatureCollection", features });
  const path0  = d3.geoPath().projection(proj0);

  // SSP column headers
  const colHeaders = htl.html`<div style="display:flex;gap:2px;margin-left:${labelW}px;margin-bottom:2px;">
    ${ssps.map(s => htl.html`<div style="width:${facetW}px;text-align:center;font-size:10px;font-weight:bold;color:#333;">${sspLabels[s]}</div>`)}
  </div>`;

  // Grid rows
  const gridRows = thresholds.map(t => {
    const cells = ssps.map(s => {
      const sRows   = byScenario.get(s) ?? [];
      const byKey   = d3.group(sRows, joinKey);
      const crossing = new Map([...byKey].map(([k, rs]) => [k, firstCrossing(rs, t)]));

      const svg = d3.create("svg")
        .attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${facetW} ${facetH}`)
        .attr("width", facetW).attr("height", facetH)
        .style("border", "1px solid #888")
        .style("background", "#fff");
      const g = svg.append("g").attr("transform", "translate(6, 4)");

      // Pass 1: all country admin1 boundaries as grey outlines (always visible).
      for (const f of countryFeatures) {
        g.append("path").attr("d", path0(f))
          .attr("fill", selAdmin1.length > 0 ? "#f5f5f5" : "none")
          .attr("stroke", "#888").attr("stroke-width", 0.5);
      }
      // Pass 2: selected (or all when no selection) filled with threshold colour — no stroke here.
      for (const f of features) {
        const cross = crossing.get(f.properties[featureProp]) ?? null;
        g.append("path").attr("d", path0(f))
          .attr("fill", periodColours[cross]).attr("stroke", "none")
          .append("title")
          .text(`${f.properties[featureProp]}: ${periodLabels[cross ?? null]}`);
      }
      // Pass 3: all boundary lines on top of everything — always visible.
      for (const f of countryFeatures) {
        g.append("path").attr("d", path0(f))
          .attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", "#888").attr("stroke-width", 0.5);
      }
      return svg.node();
    });

    return htl.html`<div style="display:flex;gap:2px;align-items:center;margin-bottom:2px;">
      <div style="width:${labelW}px;font-size:10px;font-weight:bold;color:#c00;text-align:right;padding-right:6px;">≥+${t}°C</div>
      ${cells}
    </div>`;
  });

  // Shared legend
  const legSvg = d3.create("svg").attr("width", width).attr("height", 24);
  let lx = labelW;
  for (const [p, label] of Object.entries(periodLabels)) {
    legSvg.append("rect").attr("x", lx).attr("y", 5).attr("width", 11).attr("height", 11)
      .attr("fill", periodColours[p]).attr("stroke", "#aaa").attr("stroke-width", 0.5);
    legSvg.append("text").attr("x", lx+14).attr("y", 14).attr("font-size", 9).attr("fill", "#333")
      .text(label);
    lx += label.length * 5.2 + 26;
  }

  return chartDownloadMenu(
    htl.html`<div>
      <p style="font-size:0.83em;color:#777;margin:2px 0 4px;">
        ${scope} · ${variable} · ${season} season · vs 1995–2014 baseline
      </p>
      ${colHeaders}
      ${gridRows}
      ${legSvg.node()}
      <p style="font-size:0.78em;color:#888;font-style:italic;margin:6px 0 0;max-width:980px;line-height:1.4;">
        <strong>Reading note:</strong> First period in which the <em>ensemble-mean</em> CMIP6 anomaly
        exceeds the threshold. Individual GCMs cross thresholds 1–2 decades earlier or later than the
        mean — this map understates the inter-model spread. For SSP1-2.6, low-threshold (+1 °C)
        crossings may be transient (the ensemble mean can drop back below later in the century); the
        map shows <em>first</em>, not <em>sustained</em>, exceedance.
      </p>
    </div>`,
    { filename: `cr097_threshold_${scope}_${variable}` }
  );
  });
}
```

```{ojs}
// Quick insight — template-driven body for CR097.
quickInsightCR097 = (() => {
  const t = nbText.sections.cr097.quickInsight;
  if (!cr097_data || !cr097_data.length) return _lang(t.loading);
  const ssps = Array.isArray(cr097_controls.ssp) && cr097_controls.ssp.length ? cr097_controls.ssp : ["ssp245"];
  const thresholds = Array.isArray(cr097_controls.threshold) && cr097_controls.threshold.length ? cr097_controls.threshold : [1.5];
  const ssp = ssps.includes("ssp245") ? "ssp245" : ssps[0];
  const thr = thresholds.includes(1.5) ? 1.5 : thresholds[0];
  const sspLab = ({ ssp126:"SSP1-2.6", ssp245:"SSP2-4.5", ssp370:"SSP3-7.0", ssp585:"SSP5-8.5" })[ssp] ?? ssp;
  const byKey = d3.group(cr097_data.filter(d => d.scenario === ssp), d => d.admin1_name);
  const total = byKey.size;
  if (!total) return Lang.reduceReplaceTemplateItems(_lang(t.noAdmin), [{ name: "ssp", value: sspLab }]);
  let early = 0, mid = 0, late = 0, never = 0;
  for (const [, rs] of byKey) {
    const sorted = [...rs].sort((a, b) => a.period.localeCompare(b.period));
    const cross = sorted.find(d => Number(d.pmean) >= thr)?.period ?? null;
    if (cross == null) never++;
    else if (cross === "2021-2040") early++;
    else if (cross === "2041-2060") mid++;
    else late++;
  }
  return Lang.reduceReplaceTemplateItems(_lang(t.ok), [
    { name: "ssp",   value: sspLab },
    { name: "thr",   value: thr },
    { name: "sum",   value: early + mid },
    { name: "total", value: total },
    { name: "pct",   value: ((early + mid) / total * 100).toFixed(0) },
    { name: "never", value: never },
  ]);
})();
```

```{ojs}
viewof periodMaps_controls = {
  const sspLabels = { ssp126:"SSP1-2.6", ssp245:"SSP2-4.5", ssp370:"SSP3-7.0", ssp585:"SSP5-8.5" };
  const _ssp     = Inputs.checkbox(["ssp126","ssp245","ssp370","ssp585"],
                     { label: "Scenarios (rows)", value: ["ssp126","ssp245","ssp370","ssp585"],
                       format: v => sspLabels[v] });
  const _var     = Inputs.select(cmip6FutureVariableValues,
                     { label: "Variable", value: "TAVG",
                       format: cmip6FutureVariableFormat });
  // Single-season dropdown — matches the other sections' convention.
  // In table mode the table shows one row per SSP for this single season;
  // Pete switches season to compare seasonal behaviour rather than
  // stacking multiple seasons in one table.
  const _season  = Inputs.select(cmip6SeasonValues,
                     { label: "Season", value: "annual", format: cmip6SeasonFormat });
  // Render mode: choropleth grid OR numerical table. Mirrors the
  // "Show table instead of map" pattern in CR-097.
  const _showTable = Inputs.toggle({
    label: "Show as table (numerical summary)",
    value: false });
  // What to colour cells by:
  //   "mean"  — ensemble-mean anomaly (the forced response).
  //   "sd"    — inter-model SD (model disagreement; sequential palette).
  const _stat    = Inputs.radio(["mean","sd"],
                     { label: "Statistic", value: "mean",
                       format: v => v === "mean" ? "Mean anomaly (forced response)" : "Inter-model SD (model disagreement)" });
  // Anomaly vs raw values. Raw (`mean` column) ships in the cache already
  // so toggling here costs zero bandwidth. Anomaly mode = ensemble-mean
  // anomaly vs 1995-2014 baseline; raw mode = ensemble-mean absolute value
  // (TAVG in °C, PTOT in mm, etc.). Matches the "Show as anomaly" toggle
  // convention used in the observational sections (P1, P3).
  const _showAnomaly = Inputs.toggle({
    label: "Show as anomaly (vs 1995-2014 baseline)",
    value: true });
  // Fade admin1s whose |ensemble-mean| < inter-model SD (Knutti & Sedláček
  // 2013 SNR diagnostic; under a Gaussian assumption corresponds to ≳84%
  // sign agreement — close to AR6 Method A's 80% sign-agreement threshold).
  // Default ON. Matches the fade-non-significant pattern used in P6
  // observational decade maps so the visual idiom is consistent across
  // the notebook.
  const _agreement = Inputs.toggle({
    label: "Fade where models disagree (|mean| < SD ≈ <84% sign agreement)",
    value: true });

  const form = htl.html`<div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:10px;align-items:flex-start;">
    <div style="min-width:200px;flex:1 1 200px;">${_ssp}</div>
    <div style="min-width:140px;flex:1 1 140px;">${_var}</div>
    <div style="min-width:200px;flex:1 1 200px;">${_season}</div>
    <div style="min-width:240px;flex:1 1 240px;">${_showAnomaly}</div>
    <div style="min-width:240px;flex:1 1 240px;">${_showTable}</div>
    <div style="min-width:220px;flex:1 1 220px;">${_stat}</div>
    <div style="min-width:260px;flex:1 1 260px;">${_agreement}</div>
  </div>`;
  Object.defineProperty(form, "value", {
    get: () => ({ ssp: _ssp.value, variable: _var.value, season: _season.value,
                  stat: _stat.value, fadeLowAgreement: _agreement.value,
                  valueMode: _showAnomaly.value ? "anomaly" : "raw",
                  showTable: _showTable.value }),
  });
  return form;
}
```

```{ojs}
// In-memory filter on the shared `cmip6_future_data` cache — no parquet
// refetch when the user changes variable / season / SSP / statistic /
// stipple toggle. The shared cell pulls every (admin1, scenario, hazard,
// season, period) row once per scope change; this filter just narrows it.
periodMaps_data = {
  if (!periodMapsVisible) return [];
  if (!cmip6_future_data.length) return [];
  const { variable, season, ssp } = periodMaps_controls;
  const ssps = Array.isArray(ssp) && ssp.length ? ssp : ["ssp245"];
  const sspSet = new Set(ssps);
  // Single-season filter (Pete reverted from multi-checkbox to dropdown).
  // Keep historical rows so the table mode can render the 1995-2014
  // baseline column. CR-097-style scenario filter excludes historical
  // rows for SSP-only sections automatically.
  return cmip6_future_data.filter(d =>
    d.variable === variable &&
    d.season === season &&
    (d.period === "1995-2014" ? d.scenario === "historical" : sspSet.has(d.scenario)));
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
{
  [periodMaps_controls, periodMaps_data, globalScopeInfo, globalMapLevel,
   globalAdmin1, globalTopoA1, globalTopoA0, cbMode, width];
  renderToDiv("plotPeriodMaps", () => {
  const { variable, stat, fadeLowAgreement, valueMode, showTable } = periodMaps_controls;
  const isRawMode = valueMode === "raw";
  const { isCountry, iso3List, scope }      = globalScopeInfo;
  const ssps      = Array.isArray(periodMaps_controls.ssp) && periodMaps_controls.ssp.length
    ? periodMaps_controls.ssp : ["ssp245"];
  const sspLabels = { ssp126:"SSP1-2.6", ssp245:"SSP2-4.5", ssp370:"SSP3-7.0", ssp585:"SSP5-8.5" };
  const sspColours = cbMode
    ? { ssp126:"#0072B2", ssp245:"#009E73", ssp370:"#E69F00", ssp585:"#D55E00" }
    : { ssp126:"#173c66", ssp245:"#f69320", ssp370:"#df0000", ssp585:"#800000" };
  // Map mode uses 4 future periods (chart cells). Table mode adds the
  // 1995-2014 baseline column as a reference row at the left.
  const periods   = ["2021-2040","2041-2060","2061-2080","2081-2100"];
  const tablePeriods = ["1995-2014", ...periods];
  // Single-season dropdown (matches the other sections). Both modes use
  // this one season; table-mode rendering iterates [season] for the row
  // loop so the structure mirrors the multi-season pattern minimally.
  const season    = typeof periodMaps_controls.season === "string"
    ? periodMaps_controls.season : "annual";
  const seasonList = [season];
  const isPTOT    = variable === "PTOT";
  const unit      = isPTOT ? "mm" : "°C";

  if (!periodMaps_data || !periodMaps_data.length) return htl.html`<p style="color:#888;font-style:italic;padding:12px 0;">
    ⏳ Fetching CMIP6 future-projection parquets (DuckDB-WASM, ~20 MB across 4 files — may take 15–30 s)…
  </p>`;

  // ============================================================
  // TABLE MODE — numerical summary (former Period table section).
  // Renders early-return so the map branch below stays untouched.
  // ============================================================
  if (showTable) {
    // Aggregate to (scenario, season, period) → spatial-mean of admin1
    // mean/anomaly + spatial-mean of sd_anomaly (model-spread proxy).
    const selAdmin1Tbl = isCountry ? (globalAdmin1 ?? []) : [];
    const adminFilterTbl = selAdmin1Tbl.length > 0
      ? d => selAdmin1Tbl.includes(d.admin1_name)
      : () => true;
    const aggTbl = new Map();
    for (const d of periodMaps_data) {
      if (!adminFilterTbl(d)) continue;
      const scenarioKey = d.period === "1995-2014" ? "historical" : d.scenario;
      const key = `${scenarioKey}|${d.season}|${d.period}`;
      if (!aggTbl.has(key)) aggTbl.set(key, { mSum: 0, sSum: 0, n: 0 });
      const m = Number(d[isRawMode ? "mean" : "mean_anomaly"]);
      const s = Number(d.sd_anomaly);
      if (!Number.isFinite(m)) continue;
      const row = aggTbl.get(key);
      row.mSum += m;
      row.sSum += Number.isFinite(s) ? s : 0;
      row.n   += 1;
    }
    const cellOfTbl = (scenarioKey, ssn, prd) => {
      const r = aggTbl.get(`${scenarioKey}|${ssn}|${prd}`);
      if (!r || !r.n) return null;
      return { mean: r.mSum / r.n, sd: r.sSum / r.n, n: r.n };
    };
    const fmtTbl = v => {
      if (v == null || !Number.isFinite(v)) return "—";
      const absV = Math.abs(v);
      const dp = (isPTOT && absV >= 10) ? 0 : 2;
      const sign = (!isRawMode && v > 0) ? "+" : "";
      return sign + v.toFixed(dp);
    };
    const th    = `padding:6px 10px;font-size:0.78em;font-weight:700;text-align:center;background:#f3f3f3;border-bottom:2px solid #888;color:#222;white-space:nowrap;`;
    const thLft = `${th}text-align:left;background:#f6f6f6;`;
    const td    = `padding:5px 10px;font-size:0.85em;text-align:center;border-bottom:1px solid #eee;white-space:nowrap;`;
    const tdLft = `${td}text-align:left;font-weight:600;`;

    // ---- Heat-map shading for future-period cells -----------------
    // Two-axis variable-awareness:
    //   1. `SCALE_FLOOR` — minimum-meaningful range per variable. Actual
    //      scaleMax = max(data range, floor). Keeps weak-signal tables
    //      pale instead of falsely saturated; prevents PTOT cells (mm-
    //      scale) collapsing to uniform alpha at a too-small fixed
    //      anchor.
    //   2. `SHADE_PALETTE` — sign-to-colour mapping. Temperatures use
    //      coral-warm / teal-cool. Precipitation + SPEI use teal-wet /
    //      amber-dry. Heat-day / water-stress / flooding indices use
    //      coral-more / teal-less (more = bad). NDD (dry-day count)
    //      flips: more dry days = drying = amber.
    // Variable lookup tables — SPEI / NDD intentionally omitted because
    // those don't ship in the CMIP6 future-projection parquet (SPEI is
    // observational-only; NDD not in the main-notebook hazard list).
    // See `cmip6FutureVariableValues` for the canonical projection-side
    // variable set.
    const SCALE_FLOOR = {
      TAVG:      2.0,   // °C
      TMAX:      2.5,
      TMIN:      2.5,
      PTOT:      100,   // mm/month
      NTx35:     15,    // days/yr
      NTx40:     15,
      NDWS:      30,
      NDWL0:     15,
      "THI-max": 5,
      "HSH-max": 100,   // hours/yr (heat-stress hours — rough proposal floor)
    };
    const SHADE_PALETTE = {
      // Temperatures: positive = warming → coral; negative = cooling → teal.
      TAVG: { positive: "216, 90, 48",  negative: "29, 158, 117" },
      TMAX: { positive: "216, 90, 48",  negative: "29, 158, 117" },
      TMIN: { positive: "216, 90, 48",  negative: "29, 158, 117" },
      // Precipitation: positive = wetter → teal (cool); negative = drier
      // → coral (hot). Same coral used for temperature warming so the
      // **hot = dry / cool = wet** convention reads visually consistent
      // across the notebook (variable is read from the row label).
      PTOT:      { positive: "29, 158, 117", negative: "216, 90, 48" },
      // Heat / water-stress / flood indices: more = bad → coral.
      NTx35:     { positive: "216, 90, 48",  negative: "29, 158, 117" },
      NTx40:     { positive: "216, 90, 48",  negative: "29, 158, 117" },
      NDWS:      { positive: "216, 90, 48",  negative: "29, 158, 117" },
      NDWL0:     { positive: "216, 90, 48",  negative: "29, 158, 117" },
      "THI-max": { positive: "216, 90, 48",  negative: "29, 158, 117" },
      "HSH-max": { positive: "216, 90, 48",  negative: "29, 158, 117" },
      _default:  { positive: "216, 90, 48",  negative: "29, 158, 117" },
    };
    const paletteFor = (v) => SHADE_PALETTE[v] ?? SHADE_PALETTE._default;
    // Data-driven scaleMax: max(|cell.mean|) across the visible future-period
    // cells, floored at the variable's minimum-meaningful range. Computed
    // once per render — see `visibleFutureCells` collection below the table
    // aggregation loop.
    const periodTableScaleMax = (visibleCells, vKey) => {
      const dataMax = Math.max(0, ...visibleCells.map(c => Math.abs(c?.mean ?? 0)));
      const floor   = SCALE_FLOOR[vKey] ?? 1;
      return Math.max(dataMax, floor);
    };
    const periodCellShade = (v, scaleMax, palette) => {
      if (v == null || Number.isNaN(v)) return "transparent";
      const val = Number(v);
      // Dead zone near zero — small noise around baseline shouldn't tint.
      if (Math.abs(val) < scaleMax * 0.02) return "transparent";
      // alphaMax kept conservative (0.55) so dark text stays readable
      // on the most-saturated cells. Higher values made the SSP5-8.5 /
      // 2081-2100 cells unreadable with grey ± suffix text.
      const alphaMax = 0.55;
      const a = Math.min(alphaMax, (Math.abs(val) / scaleMax) * alphaMax + 0.05);
      const rgb = val >= 0 ? palette.positive : palette.negative;
      return `rgba(${rgb}, ${a.toFixed(2)})`;
    };
    // Collect every cell that the body will actually shade (= future
    // periods only) so `periodTableScaleMax` sees the same data the
    // user sees. Baseline column is excluded (always ~0, would only
    // depress scaleMax for no benefit).
    const visibleFutureCells = ssps.flatMap(sc =>
      seasonList.flatMap(ssn =>
        periods.map(p => cellOfTbl(sc, ssn, p)).filter(Boolean)));
    const shadeScaleMax = periodTableScaleMax(visibleFutureCells, variable);
    const shadePalette  = paletteFor(variable);
    const headerRowTbl = htl.html`<tr>
      <th style="${thLft}">Scenario</th>
      <th style="${thLft}">Season</th>
      ${tablePeriods.map(p => htl.html`<th style="${th}">${p}</th>`)}
    </tr>`;
    const bodyRowsTbl = ssps.flatMap(sc =>
      seasonList.map(ssn => {
        const cellsTbl = tablePeriods.map(p => {
          const c = cellOfTbl(p === "1995-2014" ? "historical" : sc, ssn, p);
          if (!c) return htl.html`<td style="${td}">—</td>`;
          const robust = !isRawMode && Math.abs(c.mean) >= Math.max(c.sd, 1e-9);
          const isBaseline = p === "1995-2014";
          // Heat-map shading: only future-period anomaly cells get
          // tinted. Baseline column stays neutral grey; raw-view cells
          // stay transparent (divergent shading needs a signed zero).
          const bg = isBaseline
            ? "#fafafa"
            : (isRawMode ? "transparent" : periodCellShade(c.mean, shadeScaleMax, shadePalette));
          const isTinted = !isBaseline && !isRawMode && bg !== "transparent";
          // On tinted backgrounds force dark text (#111) for both
          // robust and non-robust cells — readability beats the grey-
          // for-non-robust subtle cue (which is still carried by the
          // bold weight on robust cells). On untinted cells keep the
          // grey-for-non-robust contrast.
          const color = isBaseline
            ? "#666"
            : (isTinted ? "#111" : (robust ? "#111" : "#888"));
          const fw    = isBaseline ? "500" : (robust ? "700" : "500");
          // ± SD suffix — darker on tinted cells so it stays legible
          // against the saturated background (was #888 → invisible on
          // dark teal).
          const sdColor = isTinted ? "#333" : "#888";
          const sdSuffix = isRawMode
            ? ""
            : htl.html`<span style="font-size:0.85em;color:${sdColor};font-weight:400;"> ± ${c.sd.toFixed(2)}</span>`;
          return htl.html`<td style="${td};color:${color};font-weight:${fw};background:${bg};">
            ${fmtTbl(c.mean)}${sdSuffix}
          </td>`;
        });
        const swatch = htl.html`<span style="display:inline-block;width:10px;height:10px;background:${sspColours[sc] ?? "#999"};border-radius:2px;margin-right:6px;vertical-align:middle;"></span>`;
        return htl.html`<tr>
          <td style="${tdLft}">${swatch}${sspLabels[sc] ?? sc}</td>
          <td style="${tdLft}">${ssn === "annual" ? "Annual" : ssn}</td>
          ${cellsTbl}
        </tr>`;
      })
    );
    const adminLabelTbl = selAdmin1Tbl.length > 0
      ? `${selAdmin1Tbl.length} admin1 selected`
      : (isCountry ? "all admin1s in country" : `all admin1s in ${scope}`);
    const tableEl = htl.html`<div style="overflow-x:auto;margin-top:6px;">
      <p style="font-size:0.83em;color:#777;margin:2px 0 6px;">
        <strong>${scope}</strong> · ${variable} · ${adminLabelTbl} · units: ${unit}
        ${isRawMode ? "(raw ensemble-mean values)" : "(anomaly vs 1995–2014 baseline)"}
      </p>
      <table style="border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;min-width:640px;">
        <thead>${headerRowTbl}</thead>
        <tbody>${bodyRowsTbl}</tbody>
      </table>
      <p style="font-size:0.78em;color:#888;font-style:italic;margin:6px 0 0;line-height:1.4;">
        ${isRawMode
          ? "Raw ensemble-mean values. 1995–2014 column = NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 historical scenario (model hindcast). Inter-model SD not shown — the parquet ships SD only for the anomaly column; switch to Anomaly view to see model spread."
          : "Bold = robust (|mean| ≥ inter-model SD, ≈ ≥84% GCM sign-agreement, see About). 1995–2014 column = NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 historical scenario (model hindcast)."}
      </p>
    </div>`;
    return chartDownloadMenu(tableEl, { filename: `period_table_${scope}_${variable}` });
  }
  // ============================================================
  // MAP MODE continues below. Uses single `season` (first selected).
  // ============================================================

  // Country → always admin1. Region → follow toggle (default admin0).
  const useAdmin1Map = isCountry ? true : (globalMapLevel === "admin1");
  const featureProp  = useAdmin1Map ? "admin1_name" : "iso3";

  // Column selector — anomaly view reads `mean_anomaly`; raw view reads
  // `mean` (absolute value). Both ship in the shared cache so flipping
  // costs zero bandwidth. SD column is always `sd_anomaly` — raw `sd` is
  // NOT in the parquet, so the fade-low-agreement test continues to use
  // the anomaly SD as the model-spread proxy.
  const meanCol = isRawMode ? "mean" : "mean_anomaly";
  // Map mode narrows the multi-season + historical-baseline cache to the
  // single season currently displayed in the grid, dropping the historical
  // rows (CR-097 + this view both fade the baseline col to a uniform 0
  // — meaningless on a map).
  const mapRows = periodMaps_data.filter(d =>
    d.season === season && d.period !== "1995-2014" && ssps.includes(d.scenario));
  // Aggregate to chosen map level. admin1 view: passthrough. admin0 view:
  // mean over admin1s per (scenario, period, iso3).
  const aggData = useAdmin1Map
    ? mapRows.map(d => ({
        join_key: d.admin1_name,
        scenario: d.scenario,
        period:   d.period,
        mean:     Number(d[meanCol]),
        sd:       Number(d.sd_anomaly),
      }))
    : [...d3.group(mapRows, d => `${d.iso3}|${d.scenario}|${d.period}`)].map(([k, rs]) => {
        const [jk, sc, pe] = k.split("|");
        return {
          join_key: jk, scenario: sc, period: pe,
          mean: d3.mean(rs, d => Number(d[meanCol])),
          sd:   d3.mean(rs, d => Number(d.sd_anomaly)),
        };
      });

  // Compute the value the cell will be coloured by per row.
  for (const r of aggData) r.value = stat === "mean" ? r.mean : r.sd;

  // Colour scale.
  //  - Mean view: diverging palette IF data crosses zero (signed range);
  //    sequential half-palette IF the visible data is one-signed (e.g. TAVG
  //    future anomalies for SSA are virtually always positive — using a
  //    full ±max-abs diverging legend wastes the negative half and
  //    confuses the reader).
  //  - SD view: always sequential [0, max].
  const vals = aggData.map(d => d.value).filter(v => Number.isFinite(v));
  if (!vals.length) return htl.html`<p style="color:#c00">No data rows after filter.</p>`;
  const vMin = d3.min(vals);
  const vMax = d3.max(vals);
  // "Effectively one-signed" tolerance: if the opposite-sign tail is < 5%
  // of the dominant tail's magnitude, treat it as a one-sided scale.
  // Only relevant for ANOMALY view — anomaly's 0 is the baseline reference
  // and anchoring the palette there is meaningful. Raw mode has no
  // semantic zero (a TAVG of 0 °C is a real temperature, not a "no
  // change" point), so we always pin to the data range there.
  const oneSidedTol = 0.05;
  const positiveOnly = stat === "mean" && !isRawMode && vMin >= -oneSidedTol * Math.max(Math.abs(vMax), 1e-6);
  const negativeOnly = stat === "mean" && !isRawMode && vMax <=  oneSidedTol * Math.max(Math.abs(vMin), 1e-6);
  const isOneSided   = positiveOnly || negativeOnly;
  const isSigned     = stat === "mean" && !isRawMode && !isOneSided;
  const maxAbs = stat === "mean"
    ? Math.max(1e-6, d3.max(vals, Math.abs))
    : d3.max(vals);
  // Domain selection:
  //   - Raw mean view → [vMin, vMax] tight (no zero anchor — see comment above).
  //   - Anomaly signed → [-maxAbs, maxAbs] (diverging, zero centred).
  //   - Anomaly negativeOnly → [-maxAbs, 0].
  //   - Anomaly positiveOnly OR SD → [0, maxAbs].
  // For raw mode we add a small pad so the extremes don't sit on the
  // palette edge — gives the eye breathing room at the saturated end.
  const colourDomain = isRawMode && stat === "mean"
      ? (() => {
          const span = vMax - vMin;
          const pad  = span === 0 ? (isPTOT ? 1 : 0.5) : span * 0.04;
          return [vMin - pad, vMax + pad];
        })()
    : isSigned     ? [-maxAbs, maxAbs]
    : negativeOnly ? [-maxAbs, 0]
    : /* pos / sd */  [0, maxAbs];
  // Interpolator selection.
  //   SD view:     sequential warm (Reds / Viridis-CB).
  //   Raw mean:    sequential, variable-aware so the **hot = dry / cool =
  //                wet** convention holds across the notebook.
  //                  - Temperature → Inferno / OrRd (high temp = hot).
  //                  - Precipitation → RdYlBu (low PTOT = red = dry,
  //                    high PTOT = blue = wet); PuBu in CB mode.
  //   Anomaly:     diverging — RdBu (temp; positive = red = warm) or
  //                BrBG (PTOT; positive = teal = wet = cool). Half-
  //                palette when the visible range is one-signed.
  const interp = (() => {
    if (stat !== "mean") return cbMode ? d3.interpolateViridis : d3.interpolateReds;
    if (isRawMode) {
      if (isPTOT) return cbMode ? d3.interpolatePuBu : d3.interpolateRdYlBu;
      return cbMode ? d3.interpolateInferno : d3.interpolateOrRd;
    }
    if (isPTOT) {
      const div = cbMode ? d3.interpolatePuOr : d3.interpolateBrBG;
      if (positiveOnly) return t => div(0.5 + 0.5 * t);   // wet half
      if (negativeOnly) return t => div(0.5 * (1 - t));    // dry half (reversed: t=0 → 0.5, t=1 → 0)
      return div;
    }
    // Temperature anomaly: RdBu (red is the LOW end of RdBu, so reverse).
    if (positiveOnly) return t => d3.interpolateRdBu(0.5 - 0.5 * t); // white → dark red
    if (negativeOnly) return t => d3.interpolateRdBu(0.5 + 0.5 * t); // white → dark blue
    return t => d3.interpolateRdBu(1 - t);                            // diverging, reversed
  })();
  const colourScale = d3.scaleSequential(colourDomain, interp);

  // Topojson features
  const allFeatures = useAdmin1Map
    ? topojson.feature(globalTopoA1,    globalTopoA1.objects["atlas_gaul24_a1_africa"]).features
    : topojson.feature(globalTopoA0, globalTopoA0.objects["atlas_gaul24_a0_africa"]).features;
  const countryFeatures = allFeatures.filter(f => iso3List.includes(f.properties.iso3));
  const selAdmin1 = useAdmin1Map ? (globalAdmin1 ?? []) : [];
  const features  = selAdmin1.length > 0
    ? countryFeatures.filter(f => selAdmin1.includes(f.properties[featureProp]))
    : countryFeatures;

  if (!features.length) return htl.html`<p style="color:#c00">
    No map features for <strong>${scope}</strong>.
  </p>`;

  // Layout: rows = SSPs, cols = 4 periods.
  const nCols  = periods.length;
  const labelW = 64;
  const facetW = Math.max(140, Math.floor((width - labelW - nCols * 2) / nCols));
  const facetH = Math.round(facetW * 0.85);
  const proj0  = d3.geoMercator().fitSize([facetW - 12, facetH - 24],
    { type: "FeatureCollection", features });
  const path0  = d3.geoPath().projection(proj0);

  // Column headers — period labels
  const colHeaders = htl.html`<div style="display:flex;gap:2px;margin-left:${labelW}px;margin-bottom:2px;">
    ${periods.map(p => htl.html`<div style="width:${facetW}px;text-align:center;font-size:10px;font-weight:bold;color:#333;">${p}</div>`)}
  </div>`;

  // Map (scenario × period) → data row, for fast lookup per cell.
  const lookup = new Map(aggData.map(d => [`${d.scenario}|${d.period}|${d.join_key}`, d]));

  // Robustness flag per admin1×SSP×period: TRUE when |ensemble-mean| ≥
  // inter-model SD. Under a Gaussian ensemble assumption this ≈ ≥84% of
  // GCMs agree on sign — close to IPCC AR6 Method A's 80% sign-agreement
  // threshold. Caveat in About: the AR6-canonical %-agreement test needs
  // per-GCM rows (CR-060) which the pipeline doesn't expose yet.
  const isRobust = row => {
    if (!row || !Number.isFinite(row.mean) || !Number.isFinite(row.sd)) return false;
    return Math.abs(row.mean) >= row.sd;
  };
  // Faded admin1s get this fill-opacity; matches P6's non-significant fade
  // (`fill-opacity: 0.22` for non-MK-sig admin1s) so the visual idiom
  // reads the same across observational + projection map sections.
  const fadeOpacity = 0.22;
  // Fade rule is anomaly-relative — disable in raw view because |raw|
  // is dominated by the climatology (e.g. TAVG 18 °C vs anomaly SD 0.5 °C
  // would trivially pass every admin1).
  const useFade = fadeLowAgreement && stat === "mean" && !isRawMode;

  const gridRows = ssps.map(sspKey => {
    const cells = periods.map(period => {
      const svg = d3.create("svg")
        .attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${facetW} ${facetH}`)
        .attr("width", facetW).attr("height", facetH)
        .style("border", "1px solid #888")
        .style("background", "#fff");
      const g = svg.append("g").attr("transform", "translate(6, 4)");

      // Pass 1: country admin1 boundaries as grey outlines.
      for (const f of countryFeatures) {
        g.append("path").attr("d", path0(f))
          .attr("fill", selAdmin1.length > 0 ? "#f5f5f5" : "none")
          .attr("stroke", "#888").attr("stroke-width", 0.4);
      }
      // Pass 2: selected features filled with colour. Low-agreement
      // admin1s fade to background; robust admin1s stay full saturation.
      for (const f of features) {
        const row  = lookup.get(`${sspKey}|${period}|${f.properties[featureProp]}`);
        const v    = row?.value;
        const fill = Number.isFinite(v) ? colourScale(v) : "#ddd";
        const robust = isRobust(row);
        const op   = useFade ? (robust ? 1.0 : fadeOpacity) : 1.0;
        g.append("path").attr("d", path0(f))
          .attr("fill", fill).attr("fill-opacity", op)
          .attr("stroke", "none")
          .append("title")
          .text(`${f.properties[featureProp]}\n${sspLabels[sspKey]} · ${period}\nmean: ${row?.mean?.toFixed(2) ?? "—"} ${unit}\nsd: ${row?.sd?.toFixed(2) ?? "—"} ${unit}\n|mean|/SD: ${(row && Number.isFinite(row.mean) && Number.isFinite(row.sd) && row.sd > 0) ? (Math.abs(row.mean) / row.sd).toFixed(2) : "—"}${robust ? " (robust ≥1)" : " (low agreement <1)"}`);
      }
      // Pass 3: boundary lines on top.
      for (const f of countryFeatures) {
        g.append("path").attr("d", path0(f))
          .attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", "#888").attr("stroke-width", 0.4);
      }
      return svg.node();
    });

    return htl.html`<div style="display:flex;gap:2px;align-items:center;margin-bottom:2px;">
      <div style="width:${labelW}px;font-size:10px;font-weight:bold;color:#333;text-align:right;padding-right:6px;">${sspLabels[sspKey]}</div>
      ${cells}
    </div>`;
  });

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Continuous colour-ramp legend. Sized so PTOT-mm tick labels (which can
  // be 5-6 digits wide) don't overlap each other and the title doesn't get
  // clipped at the top of the SVG viewbox.
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Smart tick formatter:
  //   PTOT (mm) → integer for |v| ≥ 10, 1 dp otherwise.
  //   °C        → 1 dp always.
  // Signed for mean view, unsigned for SD view.
  const fmtNum = v => {
    const absV  = Math.abs(v);
    const dp    = (isPTOT && absV >= 10) ? 0 : 1;
    // Sign prefix only for anomaly view — raw values use bare numbers.
    const sign  = (stat === "mean" && !isRawMode && v > 0) ? "+" : "";
    return sign + v.toFixed(dp);
  };
  // Tick anchors driven by the actual colourDomain so the legend matches
  // the rendered palette. Signed anomaly → 5 ticks around 0; one-signed
  // anomaly or SD → 4 ticks from 0 / nearest-to-zero edge to the max.
  // Raw view → 4 evenly spaced ticks across the data range.
  const [domLo, domHi] = colourDomain;
  const ticksRaw = (isRawMode && stat === "mean")
      ? [domLo, domLo + (domHi - domLo) / 3, domLo + 2 * (domHi - domLo) / 3, domHi]
    : isSigned
      ? [domLo, domLo / 2, 0, domHi / 2, domHi]
    : negativeOnly
      ? [domLo, (2 * domLo) / 3, domLo / 3, 0]
      : [0, domHi / 3, (2 * domHi) / 3, domHi];
  // Estimate widest tick label in px (≈6 px per char at font-size 10).
  // Local var (not `labelW`, which is already declared earlier for the
  // SSP-row label column).
  const maxLabelChars = Math.max(...ticksRaw.map(v => fmtNum(v).length));
  const tickLabelW   = maxLabelChars * 6 + 6;
  const minRampW = Math.max(320, tickLabelW * ticksRaw.length);
  const rampW    = Math.min(560, minRampW);
  const rampH    = 12;
  const titleH   = 14, tickH = 14, gap = 4;
  const totalH   = titleH + gap + rampH + gap + tickH + 2;
  const rampSvg  = d3.create("svg")
    .attr("width", rampW + 36)               // +36 = right padding for unit suffix
    .attr("height", totalH)
    .style("overflow", "visible");
  const rampId = `pm-ramp-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 7)}`;
  const defs   = rampSvg.append("defs");
  const grad   = defs.append("linearGradient").attr("id", rampId)
    .attr("x1", "0%").attr("x2", "100%");
  const nStops = 24;
  for (let i = 0; i <= nStops; i++) {
    const t   = i / nStops;
    const dom = domLo + t * (domHi - domLo);
    grad.append("stop").attr("offset", `${t * 100}%`).attr("stop-color", colourScale(dom));
  }

  // Title — fully above ramp with breathing room.
  const legendLabel = stat === "mean"
    ? (isRawMode
        ? `Ensemble-mean ${variable} (raw value, ${unit})`
        : `Ensemble-mean anomaly vs 1995–2014 baseline`)
    : `Inter-model SD across 18 GCMs`;
  rampSvg.append("text")
    .attr("x", 0).attr("y", titleH - 2)
    .attr("font-size", 11).attr("font-weight", 600).attr("fill", "#222")
    .text(legendLabel);

  // Ramp.
  const rampY = titleH + gap;
  rampSvg.append("rect")
    .attr("x", 0).attr("y", rampY).attr("width", rampW).attr("height", rampH)
    .attr("fill", `url(#${rampId})`).attr("stroke", "#888").attr("stroke-width", 0.5);

  // Tick labels (using d3 axis for clean placement + alignment).
  const tickScale = d3.scaleLinear()
    .domain(colourDomain)
    .range([0, rampW]);
  const tickValues = ticksRaw;
  const axisG = rampSvg.append("g")
    .attr("transform", `translate(0, ${rampY + rampH})`)
    .call(d3.axisBottom(tickScale).tickValues(tickValues).tickSize(4).tickFormat(fmtNum));
  axisG.selectAll("text").attr("font-size", 10).attr("fill", "#333");
  axisG.selectAll("line").attr("stroke", "#888").attr("stroke-width", 0.6);
  axisG.select(".domain").remove();

  // Unit suffix to the right of the ramp (keeps "mm" / "°C" out of the
  // tick-label row where it would crowd numeric labels).
  rampSvg.append("text")
    .attr("x", rampW + 6).attr("y", rampY + rampH - 1)
    .attr("font-size", 10).attr("font-weight", 500).attr("fill", "#555")
    .text(unit);

  // Footer note shown when the fade-low-agreement view is active. Two
  // swatches at saturated vs faded opacity, with the SNR criterion stated
  // explicitly. Knutti & Sedláček (2013) cited inline; AR6 cross-reference
  // lives in the About-this-section disclosure.
  const stippleNote = useFade
    ? htl.html`<div style="font-size:11px;color:#555;margin-top:8px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:14px;flex-wrap:wrap;">
        <span style="display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;">
          <span style="display:inline-block;width:14px;height:10px;background:#d55e00;"></span>
          <span>robust (|mean| ≥ SD, ≈ ≥84% GCM sign-agreement)</span>
        </span>
        <span style="display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;">
          <span style="display:inline-block;width:14px;height:10px;background:#d55e00;opacity:${fadeOpacity};"></span>
          <span>low agreement (|mean| &lt; SD)</span>
        </span>
        <span style="color:#888;">Signal-to-noise per Knutti &amp; Sedláček (2013); proxy for AR6 sign-agreement (see About).</span>
      </div>`
    : "";

  return chartDownloadMenu(
    htl.html`<div>
      ${colHeaders}
      ${gridRows}
      <div style="margin-top:10px;">
        ${rampSvg.node()}
        ${stippleNote}
      </div>
    </div>`,
    { filename: `period_maps_${scope}_${variable}_${stat}` }
  );
  });
}
```

```{ojs}
// Quick Insight now delegates the ranking + degradation logic to the
// shared `quickInsightExtremes` helper. This cell builds the cells
// array + the context-summary prose lead + the robustness paragraph,
// then hands off to the helper for the prose + ranking panel.
quickInsightPeriodMaps = (() => {
  const t = nbText.sections.periodMaps.quickInsight;
  if (!periodMaps_data || !periodMaps_data.length) return htl.html`<p style="margin:0;color:#888;font-style:italic;">${_lang(t.loading)}</p>`;
  const ssps   = Array.isArray(periodMaps_controls.ssp) && periodMaps_controls.ssp.length
    ? periodMaps_controls.ssp : ["ssp245"];
  // Insight focus: SSP2-4.5 mid-century (2041-2060) if available, else
  // first selected SSP. Single season pulled from the section's dropdown.
  const ssp    = ssps.includes("ssp245") ? "ssp245" : ssps[0];
  const period = "2041-2060";
  const sspLab = ({ ssp126:"SSP1-2.6", ssp245:"SSP2-4.5", ssp370:"SSP3-7.0", ssp585:"SSP5-8.5" })[ssp] ?? ssp;
  const seasonForInsight = typeof periodMaps_controls.season === "string"
    ? periodMaps_controls.season : "annual";
  const sel    = periodMaps_data.filter(d =>
    d.scenario === ssp && d.period === period && d.season === seasonForInsight);
  if (!sel.length) return htl.html`<p style="margin:0;color:#888;font-style:italic;">${_lang(t.noData)}</p>`;
  const isPTOT  = periodMaps_controls.variable === "PTOT";
  const unit    = isPTOT ? "mm" : "°C";
  // Build cells in the helper's contract: { admin1_name, mean, sd, robust }.
  const cells = sel
    .map(d => {
      const m = Number(d.mean_anomaly);
      const s = Number(d.sd_anomaly);
      const robust = Number.isFinite(s) && Math.abs(m) >= s;
      return { admin1_name: d.admin1_name, mean: m, sd: s, robust };
    })
    .filter(c => Number.isFinite(c.mean));
  if (!cells.length) return htl.html`<p style="margin:0;color:#888;font-style:italic;">${_lang(t.noData)}</p>`;
  const meanAvg = d3.mean(cells, c => c.mean);
  const robustCount = cells.filter(c => c.robust).length;
  const robustPct   = (robustCount / cells.length * 100).toFixed(0);
  // Context-summary lead — preserves the existing wording from
  // nbText.periodMaps.quickInsight.ok minus the (now-unused) min/max
  // placeholders, which the helper renders as a "Range across admin1s"
  // clause downstream.
  const proseLead = `Under **${sspLab}** in **${period}** (${seasonForInsight} season), ensemble-mean ${periodMaps_controls.variable} anomaly across **${cells.length} admin1s** in scope: **${(meanAvg >= 0 ? "+" : "") + meanAvg.toFixed(2)} ${unit}**.`;
  const proseTail = `**${robustCount} of ${cells.length} admin1s (${robustPct}%)** pass the signal-to-noise robustness test (|mean| ≥ inter-model SD ≈ ≥84% GCM sign-agreement); the rest are faded on the map above.`;
  return quickInsightExtremes({
    cells,
    variable: periodMaps_controls.variable,
    unit,
    topN: 5,
    proseLead,
    proseTail,
  });
})();
```

```{ojs}
// In-memory filter on the shared `cmip6_future_data` cache. Returns per-
// admin1 rows for the chosen variable + season for every selected SSP +
// the 1995-2014 historic baseline. Render block groups by (period, scenario)
// and overlays one ridge per scenario within each period row.
periodRidges_data = {
  if (!periodRidgesVisible) return [];
  if (!cmip6_future_data.length) return [];
  const { variable, season, ssp } = periodRidges_controls;
  const ssps = Array.isArray(ssp) && ssp.length ? ssp : ["ssp245"];
  const sspSet = new Set(ssps);
  return cmip6_future_data.filter(d =>
    d.variable === variable && d.season === season &&
    (d.period === "1995-2014" ? d.scenario === "historical" : sspSet.has(d.scenario)));
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
{
  [periodRidges_controls, periodRidges_data, globalScopeInfo, cbMode, width];
  renderToDiv("plotPeriodRidges", () => {
  const { variable, season, ssp, valueMode } = periodRidges_controls;
  const isRawMode = valueMode === "raw";
  const meanCol   = isRawMode ? "mean" : "mean_anomaly";
  const { scope }                 = globalScopeInfo;
  const isPTOT = variable === "PTOT";
  const unit   = isPTOT ? "mm" : "°C";
  const ssps   = Array.isArray(ssp) && ssp.length ? ssp : ["ssp245"];

  if (!periodRidges_data.length) return htl.html`<p style="color:#888;font-style:italic;padding:12px 0;">
    ⏳ Fetching CMIP6 parquets (shared cache — may take 15–30 s on first scroll into Future Projections)…
  </p>`;

  // Per-SSP fill colours — IPCC AR6 / NASA NEX-GDDP convention, mitigation
  // (cool tones) → high-emission (warm tones). CB mode swaps to Okabe-Ito.
  const sspLabels = { ssp126:"SSP1-2.6", ssp245:"SSP2-4.5", ssp370:"SSP3-7.0", ssp585:"SSP5-8.5" };
  const sspColours = cbMode
    ? { ssp126:"#0072B2", ssp245:"#009E73", ssp370:"#E69F00", ssp585:"#D55E00" }
    : { ssp126:"#173c66", ssp245:"#f69320", ssp370:"#df0000", ssp585:"#800000" };
  const baselineColour = "#555"; // 1995-2014 historic baseline ridge — neutral grey

  // Build (period, scenario) groups. Per-period array holds one entry per
  // SSP (plus "historical" for 1995-2014). Each entry = list of admin1
  // ensemble-mean anomalies feeding one KDE ridge.
  const periodOrder = ["1995-2014","2021-2040","2041-2060","2061-2080","2081-2100"];
  const periodGroups = new Map(periodOrder.map(p => [p, new Map()]));
  for (const r of periodRidges_data) {
    const v = Number(r[meanCol]);
    if (!Number.isFinite(v)) continue;
    if (!periodGroups.has(r.period)) continue;
    const pg = periodGroups.get(r.period);
    if (!pg.has(r.scenario)) pg.set(r.scenario, []);
    pg.get(r.scenario).push(v);
  }

  // Periods kept = those with ≥2 admin1s in ANY scenario; otherwise drop.
  const havePeriods = periodOrder.filter(p => {
    const pg = periodGroups.get(p);
    return [...pg.values()].some(arr => arr.length >= 2);
  });
  if (havePeriods.length < 2) return htl.html`<p style="color:#888;">Insufficient admin1 coverage for ridge KDE (need ≥2 admin1s per period × scenario).</p>`;

  // Shared x-domain: cover all admin1 values across every (period, scenario),
  // x-domain. Anomaly view: anchor at 0 so the baseline ridge centres
  // under "no change". Raw view: tight around the data range — values
  // don't cross zero, the zero reference is meaningless.
  const allVals = havePeriods.flatMap(p =>
    [...periodGroups.get(p).values()].flat());
  const dataMin = d3.min(allVals);
  const dataMax = d3.max(allVals);
  const xMin = isRawMode ? dataMin : Math.min(0, dataMin);
  const xMax = isRawMode ? dataMax : Math.max(0, dataMax);
  const pad  = (xMax - xMin) * 0.08 || (isPTOT ? 1 : 0.1);
  const xDomain = [xMin - pad, xMax + pad];
  const xGrid   = d3.range(xDomain[0], xDomain[1], (xDomain[1] - xDomain[0]) / 220);

  // Epanechnikov KDE + Silverman bandwidth — same algorithm as P3.
  const epan = u => Math.abs(u) <= 1 ? 0.75 * (1 - u * u) : 0;
  const bwFloor = isPTOT ? 1 : 0.05;
  function kde(values) {
    const n = values.length;
    if (n < 2) return null;
    const std = d3.deviation(values) ?? 0;
    const sorted = [...values].sort(d3.ascending);
    const iqr = d3.quantile(sorted, 0.75) - d3.quantile(sorted, 0.25);
    const bw  = Math.max(bwFloor,
                  0.9 * Math.min(std || bwFloor, (iqr || bwFloor) / 1.34) * Math.pow(n, -0.2));
    return xGrid.map(x => {
      const d = values.reduce((acc, v) => acc + epan((x - v) / bw), 0) / (n * bw);
      return { x, y: d };
    });
  }

  // Build per-period × per-scenario ridges. To keep cross-period heights
  // comparable WITHIN a period (so you can see "SSP1-2.6 narrower than
  // SSP5-8.5" inside one row), normalise each ridge by the max density
  // observed within its OWN period across all scenarios — not its own
  // peak. That preserves relative spread between scenarios in one row.
  const ridgesByPeriod = new Map();
  for (const period of havePeriods) {
    const pg = periodGroups.get(period);
    const perScenario = [];
    for (const [scenario, values] of pg) {
      const pts = kde(values);
      if (!pts) continue;
      perScenario.push({ scenario, points: pts, values });
    }
    if (!perScenario.length) continue;
    const peak = d3.max(perScenario.flatMap(s => s.points.map(p => p.y))) || 1;
    perScenario.forEach(s => {
      s.points = s.points.map(p => ({ x: p.x, y: p.y / peak }));
    });
    ridgesByPeriod.set(period, perScenario);
  }

  // Layout. Make the plot roughly square: each ridge row gets a height
  // proportional to the plot width / number of periods, so a 5-period
  // stack fills the same vertical extent as the horizontal extent.
  const marginL = 76, marginR = 18, marginT = 26, marginB = 56;
  const innerW  = Math.max(380, width - marginL - marginR);
  // Aim for innerH ≈ innerW so the plot reads square. Each row gets
  // innerW / havePeriods.length; clamp to a sensible min/max so single-
  // period scopes don't stretch unreadably tall.
  const rowH    = Math.max(72, Math.min(180, Math.floor((innerW - 10) / havePeriods.length)));
  const ridgeH  = Math.floor(rowH * 0.82);
  const innerH  = havePeriods.length * rowH + 10;
  const totalH  = marginT + innerH + marginB;
  const totalW  = marginL + innerW + marginR;

  const xScale  = d3.scaleLinear().domain(xDomain).range([0, innerW]);

  const svg = d3.create("svg")
    .attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${totalW} ${totalH}`)
    .attr("width", totalW).attr("height", totalH)
    .style("font-family", "system-ui, sans-serif")
    .style("max-width", "100%").style("height", "auto")
    .attr("id", `plotPeriodRidgesSvg`);
  const root = svg.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(${marginL}, ${marginT})`);

  // Zero-anomaly reference line — only in anomaly view; raw values rarely
  // cross zero meaningfully, so the dashed line would be misleading.
  if (!isRawMode && xDomain[0] <= 0 && xDomain[1] >= 0) {
    root.append("line")
      .attr("x1", xScale(0)).attr("x2", xScale(0))
      .attr("y1", 0).attr("y2", innerH)
      .attr("stroke", "#999").attr("stroke-width", 1)
      .attr("stroke-dasharray", "4 3");
  }

  // Draw ridges bottom-up (oldest period at bottom).
  havePeriods.forEach((period, i) => {
    const baselineY = innerH - i * rowH - ridgeH / 2;
    const perScenario = ridgesByPeriod.get(period) ?? [];

    // Render order: historical first (so it sits behind future ridges if
    // ever overlapping); then future SSPs in ssp126→ssp585 order so the
    // higher-emission scenarios (rightward-shifted) stack on top.
    const ordered = [
      ...perScenario.filter(s => s.scenario === "historical"),
      ...["ssp126","ssp245","ssp370","ssp585"]
        .flatMap(k => perScenario.filter(s => s.scenario === k)),
    ];

    for (const s of ordered) {
      const fill = s.scenario === "historical" ? baselineColour : (sspColours[s.scenario] ?? "#999");
      const area = d3.area()
        .x(d => xScale(d.x))
        .y0(baselineY)
        .y1(d => baselineY - d.y * ridgeH)
        .curve(d3.curveMonotoneX);
      const line = d3.line()
        .x(d => xScale(d.x))
        .y(d => baselineY - d.y * ridgeH)
        .curve(d3.curveMonotoneX);
      root.append("path").datum(s.points)
        .attr("d", area).attr("fill", fill).attr("fill-opacity", 0.50)
        .attr("stroke", "none");
      root.append("path").datum(s.points)
        .attr("d", line).attr("fill", "none")
        .attr("stroke", fill).attr("stroke-width", 1.1);

      // Per-scenario median: full-height vertical tick through the ridge.
      // Drawn as a thicker coloured line with a thin white halo behind it
      // so it stays visible against overlapping translucent fills from
      // other scenarios in the same row.
      const med = d3.median(s.values);
      if (Number.isFinite(med)) {
        const mx = xScale(med);
        // White halo (background) — slightly wider, slightly translucent.
        root.append("line")
          .attr("x1", mx).attr("x2", mx)
          .attr("y1", baselineY - ridgeH - 2).attr("y2", baselineY + 4)
          .attr("stroke", "#fff").attr("stroke-width", 4)
          .attr("stroke-opacity", 0.85)
          .attr("stroke-linecap", "round");
        // Coloured median line.
        root.append("line")
          .attr("x1", mx).attr("x2", mx)
          .attr("y1", baselineY - ridgeH - 2).attr("y2", baselineY + 4)
          .attr("stroke", fill).attr("stroke-width", 2.2)
          .attr("stroke-linecap", "round");
        // Small filled circle anchor at the baseline so the median's
        // colour reads unambiguously even when ridges overlap heavily.
        root.append("circle")
          .attr("cx", mx).attr("cy", baselineY + 4)
          .attr("r", 3).attr("fill", fill)
          .attr("stroke", "#fff").attr("stroke-width", 1);
      }
    }

    // Period label on LEFT.
    root.append("text")
      .attr("x", -8).attr("y", baselineY - 4)
      .attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("font-size", 11).attr("font-weight", 600)
      .attr("fill", "#222")
      .text(period);
    // n label per scenario (compact "n=X·Y·Z" line).
    const nText = ordered.map(s => `${s.values.length}`).join("·");
    root.append("text")
      .attr("x", -8).attr("y", baselineY + 10)
      .attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("font-size", 9).attr("fill", "#777")
      .text(`n=${nText}`);
  });

  // X axis.
  const xAxis = d3.axisBottom(xScale).ticks(7)
    .tickFormat(d => `${(!isRawMode && d > 0) ? "+" : ""}${d.toFixed(isPTOT ? 0 : 1)}`);
  const xAxisG = root.append("g")
    .attr("transform", `translate(0, ${innerH})`)
    .call(xAxis);
  xAxisG.selectAll("text").attr("font-size", 10);
  root.append("text")
    .attr("x", innerW / 2).attr("y", innerH + 30)
    .attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11)
    .attr("fill", "#333")
    .text(isRawMode
      ? `Ensemble-mean ${variable} — raw value (${unit})`
      : `Ensemble-mean ${variable} anomaly vs 1995–2014 baseline (${unit})`);

  // SSP swatch legend (footer row).
  const presentSSPs = ssps.filter(s => havePeriods.some(p => (periodGroups.get(p).get(s) ?? []).length >= 2));
  const legendItems = [
    { label: "1995–2014 baseline", colour: baselineColour },
    ...presentSSPs.map(s => ({ label: sspLabels[s], colour: sspColours[s] })),
  ];
  const legendG = svg.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(${marginL}, ${marginT + innerH + 44})`);
  let lx = 0;
  for (const item of legendItems) {
    legendG.append("rect")
      .attr("x", lx).attr("y", 0).attr("width", 14).attr("height", 8)
      .attr("fill", item.colour).attr("fill-opacity", 0.50)
      .attr("stroke", item.colour).attr("stroke-width", 1);
    legendG.append("text")
      .attr("x", lx + 18).attr("y", 8)
      .attr("font-size", 10).attr("fill", "#333")
      .text(item.label);
    lx += 18 + item.label.length * 6.2 + 14;
  }

  // Title above plot.
  svg.append("text")
    .attr("x", marginL).attr("y", 16)
    .attr("font-size", 11).attr("font-weight", 600).attr("fill", "#333")
    .text(`${scope} · ${variable} · ${season} season · ${ssps.length} scenario${ssps.length === 1 ? "" : "s"}`);

  return chartDownloadMenu(
    htl.html`<div>${svg.node()}</div>`,
    { filename: `period_ridges_${scope}_${variable}_${ssps.join("-")}` }
  );
  });
}
```

```{ojs}
quickInsightPeriodRidges = (() => {
  const t = nbText.sections.periodRidges.quickInsight;
  if (!periodRidges_data || !periodRidges_data.length) return _lang(t.loading);
  const { variable, ssp } = periodRidges_controls;
  const ssps = Array.isArray(ssp) && ssp.length ? ssp : ["ssp245"];
  const isPTOT = variable === "PTOT";
  const unit   = isPTOT ? "mm" : "°C";
  const sspLabels = { ssp126:"SSP1-2.6", ssp245:"SSP2-4.5", ssp370:"SSP3-7.0", ssp585:"SSP5-8.5" };
  // Highest-emission selected SSP drives the insight (canonical worst-case
  // framing). Fall back to mid-emission if user picked only low.
  const insightSSP = ["ssp585","ssp370","ssp245","ssp126"].find(s => ssps.includes(s)) ?? ssps[0];
  const sspLab = sspLabels[insightSSP] ?? insightSSP;

  // Median + IQR per period for the insight SSP; contrast baseline vs late-century.
  const valsAt = (period, scenarioPred) => periodRidges_data
    .filter(d => d.period === period && scenarioPred(d.scenario))
    .map(d => Number(d.mean_anomaly))
    .filter(Number.isFinite);
  const base = "1995-2014", late = "2081-2100";
  const bVals = valsAt(base, s => s === "historical");
  const lVals = valsAt(late, s => s === insightSSP);
  if (bVals.length < 2 || lVals.length < 2) return _lang(t.noData);

  const bSorted = [...bVals].sort(d3.ascending);
  const lSorted = [...lVals].sort(d3.ascending);
  const bMed = d3.median(bSorted), lMed = d3.median(lSorted);
  const bIQR = d3.quantile(bSorted, 0.75) - d3.quantile(bSorted, 0.25);
  const lIQR = d3.quantile(lSorted, 0.75) - d3.quantile(lSorted, 0.25);
  const delta  = lMed - bMed;
  const dir    = isPTOT ? (delta > 0 ? "wetter" : "drier") : (delta > 0 ? "warmer" : "cooler");
  const iqrDir = lIQR > bIQR ? "widens" : "narrows";

  return Lang.reduceReplaceTemplateItems(_lang(t.ok), [
    { name: "ssp",      value: sspLab },
    { name: "variable", value: variable },
    { name: "unit",     value: unit },
    { name: "base",     value: base },
    { name: "late",     value: late },
    { name: "medBase",  value: (bMed >= 0 ? "+" : "") + bMed.toFixed(2) },
    { name: "medLate",  value: (lMed >= 0 ? "+" : "") + lMed.toFixed(2) },
    { name: "delta",    value: (delta >= 0 ? "+" : "") + delta.toFixed(2) },
    { name: "dir",      value: dir },
    { name: "iqrDir",   value: iqrDir },
    { name: "iqrBase",  value: bIQR.toFixed(2) },
    { name: "iqrLate",  value: lIQR.toFixed(2) },
  ]);
})();
```

```{ojs}
viewof periodPolar_controls = {
  const sspLabels = { ssp126:"SSP1-2.6", ssp245:"SSP2-4.5", ssp370:"SSP3-7.0", ssp585:"SSP5-8.5" };
  // Multi-SSP — renders one polar-clock column per selected SSP.
  // Default = canonical mitigation vs high-emission pair so the spread
  // of futures is visible at first render. Admin1 rows come from the
  // global Admin1 popup; >6 selected = first 6 alphabetically + a note.
  const _ssp     = Inputs.checkbox(["ssp126","ssp245","ssp370","ssp585"],
                     { label: "Scenarios (columns)", value: ["ssp126","ssp585"],
                       format: v => sspLabels[v] });
  const _var     = Inputs.select(cmip6FutureVariableValues,
                     { label: "Variable", value: "TAVG",
                       format: cmip6FutureVariableFormat });
  const _showAnomaly = Inputs.toggle({
    label: "Show as anomaly (vs 1995-2014 baseline)",
    value: true });
  const form = htl.html`<div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:10px;align-items:flex-start;">
    <div style="min-width:220px;flex:1 1 220px;">${_ssp}</div>
    <div style="min-width:140px;flex:1 1 140px;">${_var}</div>
    <div style="min-width:240px;flex:1 1 240px;">${_showAnomaly}</div>
  </div>`;
  Object.defineProperty(form, "value", {
    get: () => ({ ssp: _ssp.value, variable: _var.value,
                  valueMode: _showAnomaly.value ? "anomaly" : "raw" }),
  });
  // Explicit bubble — wrapping <div> doesn't always re-fire viewof on
  // child input changes through htl.html's interpolated children. Force
  // the form to dispatch on every child-input event.
  const bubble = () => form.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true }));
  _ssp.addEventListener("input", bubble);
  _var.addEventListener("input", bubble);
  _showAnomaly.addEventListener("input", bubble);
  return form;
}
```

```{ojs}
// In-memory filter on the shared cache. Returns rows for the chosen
// variable + selected SSPs (plus the historical baseline rows). The
// render block groups by (ssp, admin1, season, period) to build the
// per-cell polar-clock subplot.
periodPolar_data = {
  if (!periodPolarVisible) return [];
  if (!cmip6_future_data.length) return [];
  const { variable, ssp } = periodPolar_controls;
  const ssps = Array.isArray(ssp) && ssp.length ? ssp : ["ssp245"];
  const sspSet = new Set(ssps);
  return cmip6_future_data.filter(d =>
    d.variable === variable &&
    (d.period === "1995-2014" ? d.scenario === "historical" : sspSet.has(d.scenario)));
}
```
